   <title>Dialogue in the dark: David Bowie meets Nina Simone at Steve McQueen's exhibition at Guggenheim Bilbao</title>
   <link>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/dialogue-in-the-dark-david-bowie-meets-nina-simone-at-steve-mcqueens-exhibition-at-guggenh</link>
   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/dialogue-in-the-dark-david-bowie-meets-nina-simone-at-steve-mcqueens-exhibition-at-guggenh</guid>
   <pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:25:40 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>Steve McQueen’s exhibition “66–76–26” at Guggenheim Bilbao Museum is a sound sculpture with no image. It is a link between the decades, the emotion of love and understanding, and it also stars David Bowie and Nina Simone.</description>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>This country aims to attract €18B in cleaner energy investment</title>
   <link>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/this-country-aims-to-attract-18b-in-cleaner-energy-investment</link>
   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/this-country-aims-to-attract-18b-in-cleaner-energy-investment</guid>
   <pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:00:17 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>Kazakhstan aims to mobilise €18 billion in investment in cleaner energy through its just energy transition platform, QaJET, with support from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).</description>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>Angolan-Portuguese singer IAMDDB accuses Israel of stealing her identity in AI video</title>
   <link>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/angolan-portuguese-singer-iamddb-accuses-israel-of-stealing-her-identity-in-ai-video</link>
   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/angolan-portuguese-singer-iamddb-accuses-israel-of-stealing-her-identity-in-ai-video</guid>
   <pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 14:54:29 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>Angolan-Portuguese artist IAMDDB has condemned the unauthorised use of her likeness in an AI-generated propaganda video shared by Israel's official social media accounts. The Manchester-based singer accuses the government of using her image without permission.</description>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>No evidence foreign powers sparked Europe’s riots, but they exploited them</title>
   <link>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/france-and-italy-blame-foreign-powers-for-riots-but-wheres-the-evidence</link>
   <guid>https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/21/france-and-italy-blame-foreign-powers-for-riots-but-wheres-the-evidence</guid>
   <pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 14:30:09 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>There is so far no evidence that foreign powers caused Europe’s riots, only that they exploited them, despite politicians blaming online manipulation for them. Brussels has refused to act, citing a lack of evidence.</description>
  </item>
  <item>
   <title>EU probes whether Booking.com is doing enough to tackle fake listings and phishing scams</title>

   <pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 14:12:34 +0200</pubDate>
   <description>There is no fixed legal deadline for the investigation to conclude, but Booking.com can propose measures to address the European Commission's concerns.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Severely ill ICE detainees targeted for imminent deportation in Florida, advocates say</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida</link>
      <description><p>Flights to unknown countries in Africa are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail</p><p>Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</a> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">immigration</a> jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.</p><p>Flights are scheduled as early as Wednesday, according to the families and the immigration advocacy group the Workers Circle, which has been monitoring conditions and speaking with detainees inside two <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)</a> facilities in south Florida.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/florida">Florida</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/usimmigration">US immigration</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ice-us-immigration-and-customs-enforcement">ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement)</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-news">US news</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/africa">Africa</category>
      <pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:40:08 GMT</pubDate>
      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/21/ice-detention-illness-deportation-florida</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5a1fa2211f8394d63f3fcf24e563458a5818c40d/197_0_2203_1763/master/2203.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=06b2c45462af36f0767e7c85a990df76">
        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Pedro Portal/Miami Herald via Getty Images</media:credit>
      </media:content>
      <media:content width="460" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5a1fa2211f8394d63f3fcf24e563458a5818c40d/197_0_2203_1763/master/2203.jpg?width=460&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=428381e61ab382ad12dee59320e2ab9e">
        <media:credit scheme="urn:ebu">Photograph: Pedro Portal/Miami Herald via Getty Images</media:credit>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/rfk-jr-vaccine-researchers-offices-raided-guinea-bissau</link>
      <description><p>Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns</p><p>Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials <a href="https://www.facebook.com/policiajudiciariaguinebissau/posts/pfbid02x8etNUtmPjenMNZA69EHECDBcz6U4VzxTvszdthBmFmJ1aaCMwoT9brgRNYyg1Jbl">said</a> on Facebook.</p><p>The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/rfk-jr-vaccine-researchers-offices-raided-guinea-bissau">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan</link>
      <description><p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a></description>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>en</language><title>France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines</title><description>Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:44:42 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>South African former police chief accused of sex trafficking denied bail</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261021-south-african-former-police-chief-accused-of-sex-trafficking-denied-bail</link><description>
South Africa's former deputy national commissioner, Shadrack Sibiya, has been denied bail. He is facing charges of rape, trafficking and is accused of sexually grooming a child. Investigators had argued that his accusers would be in danger if he was let out. FRANCE 24's correspondent Eunice Masson reports.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3f272878-cd51-11f1-844d-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-7cd460dc.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3f272878-cd51-11f1-844d-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-7cd460dc.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">18493d92-cd4f-11f1-b3a0-1773a65f3b01</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:44:25 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>REPLAY: French union leaders urges strikes after meeting with PM Lecornu</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/replay-french-union-leaders-urges-strikes-after-meeting-with-pm-lecornu</link><description>
The leader of France's hardline CGT union on Wednesday called for strikes after talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu over fresh protests collapsed. As the country is reeling from last weekend's riots, the government offered "no measure or an acknowledgement of our demands" Sophie Binet, secretary general of the CGT, told reporters after a meeting between Lecornu and union leaders.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/756cd872-cd4e-11f1-837a-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261021-130835-132941-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/756cd872-cd4e-11f1-837a-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261021-130835-132941-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7aedbe42-cd4e-11f1-982f-21bb7d841a71</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:30:24 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Nigeria records its first Ebola case amid rapid regional spread</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261021-nigeria-records-its-first-ebola-case-amid-rapid-regional-spread</link><description>
After Kenya and Uganda, Nigeria has now announced its first Ebola case – a woman who was admitted to a private hospital in Abuja and travelled from Uganda. The outbreak, which originated in DR Congo in May, has been described by health officials as ​thefastest-spreading on record. Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent Sam Olukoya.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/48a63b76-cd53-11f1-9c1d-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-21T045618Z-1772179031-RC2G4OAZODI8-RTRMADP-3-HEALTH-EBOLA-NIGERIA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/48a63b76-cd53-11f1-9c1d-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-21T045618Z-1772179031-RC2G4OAZODI8-RTRMADP-3-HEALTH-EBOLA-NIGERIA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">da5056e4-cd4c-11f1-b5cb-6968c0ef0e51</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:28:52 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Entre Nous</category><title>What makes a great Halloween cake?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/entre-nous/20261021-what-makes-a-great-halloween-cake</link><description>
With Halloween around the corner we are pleased to welcome cake decoration expert Galina Duverne from the École de Cake Design in Paris. Galina tells us what makes a great Halloween cake and how the French have slowly been seduced by cake decorating. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0fb3ce50-cd49-11f1-a4ff-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-420820dd.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0fb3ce50-cd49-11f1-a4ff-19980254bb31/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-420820dd.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">af7a2c0c-cd1e-11f1-a84c-3546e092370e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:28:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Delano D’SOUZA</dc:creator></item><item><category>Tête à tête</category><title>US sanctions on ICC are 'a shock' and 'unacceptable', Nobel peace laureate Navi Pillay says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/t%C3%AAte-%C3%A0-t%C3%AAte/20261021-us-sanctions-on-icc-are-a-shock-and-unacceptable-nobel-peace-laureate-navi-pillay-says</link><description>
In an interview with FRANCE 24, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Navi Pillay described the US sanctions imposed on the International Criminal Court (ICC) hours after her award as "a shock" and "unacceptable". The South African judge also defended the UN commission of inquiry she chaired which concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza: "We didn't come to that conclusion lightly." Rejecting claims that the ICC targets Africa, she said "the court is not selective".

      <description>The images of France’s riots posted and broadcast around the world have cast a pall on the country’s important tourism sector, with many fearing worse consequences if violence returns.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ When will SpaceX and Blue Origin fly to the moon? NASA reveals lunar lander timelines (and an Artemis III update) ]]> NASA has revealed new details about its plans to return astronauts to the surface of the moon, outlining a series of upcoming milestones for SpaceX and Blue Origin as both companies race to ready their lunar landers for the agency's Artemis program.

During an Oct. 5 presentation at the Astronautical Congress (IAC) in Antalya, Türkiye, Steve Creech, acting manager of NASA's Human Landing System (HLS) Program, laid out development timelines for both spacecraft, with key demonstrations planned through early 2028 that include orbital refueling and uncrewed lunar landing tests to qualify the vehicles to fly astronauts to the surface of the moon.

A more pressing deadline, however, is NASA's Artemis III mission, which is targeted for the third quarter (Q3) of 2027. Artemis III will launch four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft to low Earth orbit (LEO), where they will rendezvous and dock with test versions of both companies' landers for interoperability checkouts. Those demonstrations will help inform NASA's determination about which lander the agency will choose to carry astronauts to the moon's surface on Artemis IV, targeted for early 2028.

SpaceX and Blue Origin were both awarded NASA contracts to develop HLS vehicles — Starship and Blue Moon, respectively — and have spent the past several years refining their respective lunar lander designs and dealing with various delays along the way. In the face of those delays, and in an effort to better structure its mission progression for success, NASA overhauled its Artemis program architecture in February to maintain its goal of landing astronauts on the moon by the end of 2028 and establish a more regular cadence of uncrewed landings in the meantime.

As part of that shakeup, Artemis III, previously the program's first crewed lunar landing mission, was moved up a year and repurposed for the lunar lander vehicle tests the agency is preparing to fly to LEO next year. The program's first moon landing remains scheduled for 2028, but was shifted to the manifest for Artemis IV.

Between now and then, both SpaceX and Blue Origin have more than a dozen test demonstrations and vehicle milestones to achieve, including success during Artemis III and flights afterward. This will all lead up to a key decision NASA must make: Which vehicle will carry out the first crewed landing on the surface of the moon since the Apollo program ended in 1972?

Starship reached for the first time on its most recent test flight, which occurred on Sept. 28 from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. NASA lists several other important goals for the vehicle to achieve in 2026, including (in the order listed during the IAC presentation) the first return and catch of the rocket's upgraded Version 3 (V3) booster at its launch pad; the first-ever return and catch of a Ship upper stage; the first Starship launch from one of SpaceX's launch pads still under construction on Florida's Space Coast; and, possibly, the first V3 booster reflight.

NASA also expects SpaceX to complete the initial build of the crew cabin for its lunar lander Starship variant. SpaceX released renders of Starship's interior last year, as well as images of the test elevator astronauts are using to train for Starship egress on the lunar surface, but little else has been made public about the progress the company has made on the cabin's design.

Should the cabin's initial build wrap up by the end of the year, as NASA's presentation suggested, SpaceX will use Q1 2027 to complete integration of the systems that Starship will need to communicate with Orion during Artemis III, and deliver a cabin simulator for astronauts to train on leading up to the mission. SpaceX plans to continue Starship test flights through Q2 of next year, complete a landing leg demonstration and begin crew cabin airlock tests.

Blue Origin's lunar lander mockup is ready for NASA Artemis astronaut training

For Artemis III, SpaceX plans to fly one of its existing V3 Starship upper stages, with some slight modifications. Starship and Orion will dock as part of Artemis III but the SpaceX vehicle won't be equipped with a crew cabin for the mission's astronauts to enter. Between the end of this year and the beginning of the next, SpaceX is expected to complete the addition of a docking system and nosecone cover to the Artemis III Starship vehicle, which, NASA documents suggest, has already completed its mechanical fit checks.

Other notches on SpaceX's checklist leading up to Artemis III include the first propellant transfer demonstration with Starship in orbit. As the first-ever launch vehicle and spacecraft designed for full reusability, Starship's fuel constraints require that its tanks be topped off in order to fly beyond LEO. For a moon landing mission, this could mean up to a dozen launches of SpaceX's Starship "tanker" spacecraft to an orbiting fuel depot, which the moon-bound Starship will visit. To pull that off, though, SpaceX has to show it can successfully transfer those cryogenic fuels on orbit, and also store them effectively enough to prevent too much boil-off.

Starship won't require any refueling flights to complete its objectives for Artemis III, but SpaceX is expected to launch its first Starship tanker vehicle within a few months of that mission as it gears up for the Artemis IV moon landing mission. To that end, a launch of an uncrewed Starship lunar lander variant is targeted sometime toward the end of Q3/beginning of Q4, with an uncrewed lunar landing mission carried out before the end of 2027.

Blue Origin, meanwhile, has its own set of milestones to meet as it develops its Blue Moon Mark 2 (MK2) lander — a 52-foot-tall (16 meters) spacecraft powered by three BE-7 engines. Unlike the bare-bones V3 Starship that SpaceX will launch on Artemis III, Blue Origin plans to fly a completed test vehicle, incorporating the crew cabin, partial life-support, flight software and other systems needed to allow astronauts to enter the lander from Orion during their time docked in LEO. Astronauts will be able to enter Blue Moon from Orion to get a feel for the lander in zero-g and test some of its systems.

NASA's timeline shows the company working to complete a series of manufacturing and testing milestones in the last few months of 2026, including continued BE-7 testing and qualification of Blue Moon's BT-7 maneuvering thrusters. The company also faces its Artemis III interim design review and a critical design review for an upcoming landing demonstration mission in 2028.

Blue Origin is also working to restore its pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station's Launch Complex-36 (LC-36) to operation and return its New Glenn rocket to flight, following an explosion of the rocket in May that caused extensive damage to the facility. NASA's presentation places that milestone in Q4 2026, a timeline the company has also been very vocal about maintaining. A recent Reuters report, however, suggests that may not happen until early 2027.

By early 2027, the company expects to complete the spacecraft's communications systems and finalize its flight software, with assembly, integration and testing continuing into Q2. Q1 2027 is also when Blue Origin's Blue Moon MK1 lander (a smaller, uncrewed version of its MK2 successor) will launch to the lunar surface as a part of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program of robotic moon missions.

A post shared by Space.com (@spacedotcom)

A photo posted by

During Q2 2027, as the Artemis III mission approaches, Blue Origin is expected to complete integration of its test lander with New Glenn and conclude qualification of its BE-7 engine. Throughout next year, the company plans to continue construction and refurbishments at its launch facilities and hopes to have a new launch pad ready to support the upgraded, more powerful New Glenn 9x4 rocket l by the end of Q3. The first flight of that rocket variant is scheduled for Q4 2027, alongside a second MK1 lunar mission and the launch of an uncrewed MK2 demonstration lander.

That spacecraft is expected to attempt its own uncrewed lunar landing in Q1 2028, around the same time Blue Origin has scheduled a third MK1 flight. Like SpaceX, Blue Origin will need to demonstrate that its lander can safely reach the moon's surface,operate there and return to lunar orbit before NASA clears it to carry astronauts on a future Artemis mission.

NASA's overall timeline remains the same as it has been since the February revamp, with Artemis III expected to launch in mid-2027, followed by a crewed lunar landing on Artemis IV in 2028, and possibly another on Artemis V that same year. There may be changes on the horizon, though. NASA will host a press conference on Friday (Oct. 23) with Administrator Jared Isaacman and Associate Administrator Amit Kshatriya, as well as Artemis program director Jeremy Parsons. During the event, which you'll be able to watch here at Space.com, they will discuss the status of the upcoming moon missions and an "Artemis acceleration."

SpaceX and Blue Origin still face tight schedules to complete their respective uncrewed landing demonstrations before Artemis IV. With SpaceX targeting Q4 2027 and Blue Origin Q1 2028, both are pushing the margins against NASA's hopes to return astronauts to the lunar surface that same year. Which company ultimately gets the green light for that first landing mission will depend on the progress each makes between now and then, and whether their landers can demonstrate the readiness that NASA requires to safely carry astronauts to the surface of the moon and back again.

But will the light cast by the waxing gibbous moon spoil the show?

The Orionid meteor shower activity peaks when Earth travels through the densest section of the debris trail left by Comet 1P/Halley. The comet is currently racing back towards the sun ahead of its next visit to the inner solar system in 2061.

Under perfect dark sky conditions 10 to 20 shooting stars could brighten the night sky each hour as the peak unfolds, according to NASA. However, the light cast by the waxing moon — just four days from being full — will likely reduce the number of visible meteors by hiding fainter Orionids from sight.

Orionid shooting stars will appear to travel away from a point of origin, close to the red star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion, rising above the eastern horizon an hour before midnight for viewers in the U.S.

Your best chance at spotting the fast-moving meteors will come in the hours before dawn on Oct. 22, after the moon has set and the radiant approaches its highest point in the night sky. It's best not to stare directly at the radiant, where the glowing meteor trails will be relatively short compared to those left by shooting stars that appear 45-90 degrees away from the bright star Betelgeuse, thanks to an effect known as foreshortening.

Try to travel away from city lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to adapt to the dark. Always make sure someone knows where you're going if you head somewhere remote to catch the shower and be sure to take a red light to ensure that you can find your way while also preserving your night vision!

]]> <![CDATA[ Russian satellite plays 'cat-and-mouse' with a commercial US spacecraft likely used by Ukraine. But why the risky close encounter? ]]> A Russian satellite just took a very close look at an American spacecraft in low Earth orbit.

A few days ago, the snooping satellite Kosmos 2612 rendezvoused with ICEYE-X36, a commercial craft that observes our planet using synthetic aperture radar (SAR).

The close encounter, which occurred between Oct. 15 and Oct. 19, was reported by Marco Langbroek and other satellite trackers, with Langbroek calling it "a worrisome cat-and-mouse game" in orbit. The rendezvous has garnered a lot of attention in space circles, because it was non-consensual and startlingly close; at one point, the two spacecraft may have been separated by just a few meters. What did Russia hope to gain from it?

Not an isolated incident

A worrisome cat-and-mouse-game in Space

Dr, Marco Langbroek, satellite tracker

Before tackling that question, we need to set the stage a bit. For example, it's important to note that inspections aren't unheard of in the final frontier. Russia, the United States and China have all maneuvered satellites into close proximity of other nations' hardware in recent years.

Most of this activity has taken place in geostationary orbit, which lies 22,236 miles (35,786 kilometers) above Earth. At this altitude, orbital velocity matches our planet's rotational speed, allowing spacecraft to "hover" over one patch of Earth continuously. GEO is therefore a popular destination for spy, communications and weather satellites — and for spacecraft designed to shadow and assess them.

Kosmos 2612 is operating in low Earth orbit (LEO), which is part of the reason its activities have created such a stir. Neither China nor the U.S. has conducted an uncooperative rendezvous in LEO, as far as we know. But Russia has, according to Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability for the nonprofit Secure World Foundation.

"They've done a few," she told Space.com. "Kosmos 2543 got within about 30 kilometers [19 miles] of USA 245 in January 2020, and then Kosmos 2558 got within about 70 kilometers [43 miles] of USA 326 in August 2022. And they've done repeated approaches to 326."

Kosmos 2612 got much closer to its target than those other inspectors did, of course. And there's another big difference: USA 245 and USA 326 are classified spy satellites managed by the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office, while ICEYE-X36 is a private Earth-observing craft.

Eyes in the sky

There are about 80 ICEYE spacecraft in LEO at the moment. They image our planet using SAR, which can peer through clouds and gather data both day and night. Some of these satellites are operated by ICEYE, a company based in Finland, while others are managed by its American subsidiary, ICEYE US. ICEYE-X36 is one of the latter.

At least some ICEYE satellites provide imagery to Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022 and continues to assault with ground troops and missile and drone attacks. Indeed, ICEYE signed a contract this past January firming up this data-sharing relationship with Ukraine.

"The agreement ensures that the Ministry of Defence continues to receive a high volume of high-resolution satellite imagery through ICEYE's world-leading SAR constellation, supporting the Ukrainian Armed Forces with persistent situational awareness on tactical timelines," ICEYE representatives said in a January statement.

That likely explains Russia's interest in ICEYE satellites, which is extensive and longstanding. For example, Kosmos 2612 launched in April of this year with five other spacecraft. In May, four members of this fleet, including Kosmos 2612, conducted maneuvers to get into a co-planar orbit with ICEYE-X36. Such maneuvers use a lot of fuel and are therefore not performed lightly. (It's unclear if ICEYE-X36 is dedicated to capturing imagery of Ukraine or Russia, but Russia certainly seems to think it is.)

However, we still don't know the purpose of Kosmos 2612's close approach (which is apparently over, at least for now), Samson stressed.

There are a few possibilities. For example, Russia may want to get a better idea of ICEYE satellites' capabilities, and/or figure out what exactly they're studying on Earth below. Or maybe Kosmos 2612 was actively interfering with ICEYE-X36 in some way — messing with its sensors, perhaps, or blocking or intercepting its communications with the ground.

However, Samson leans toward another explanation.

"I think they're getting frustrated," she said of the Russians.

"They've been kind of in a stalemate, particularly for the past six months or so. And so I think it's just more a matter of demonstrating military prowess in a manner that the Ukrainians cannot respond to," she added. "The Ukrainians are just as good, perhaps even better than, the Russians on drones. But when it comes to space stuff, they're not peers, and this is just a way to remind everyone that that's the case."

As Kosmos 2612's activities show, space is becoming an increasingly competitive and contested domain. The U.S. has long held the advantage above Earth, fielding the most capable reconnaissance and communications craft, but Russia and China are challenging that dominance.

This drama is unfolding above our heads now, and it affects everyone on the planet. Samson therefore wishes that governments around the world were more forthcoming about their space activities — for example, that we learned about Kosmos 2612's shenanigans from the U.S .Space Force rather than from private companies and civilians who pore over government tracking data.

"I think it just speaks to the importance of transparency, and sharing information about these sort of things," she said. "As much as you may want to, you cannot keep the existence of satellites classified, because people can see them."

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says ]]>

SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan.

The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20).

If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle. So this is, I think, a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization and consciousness."

Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall when fully stacked.

As Musk noted, both of its stages — the Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft — are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX thinks will make Mars settlement and other grand exploration feats economically feasible.

Starship's recovery strategy is different than that for SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, which are partially reusable. (The latter two rockets have expendable upper stages). Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy boosters come back to Earth on landing pads near the launch site or on ships at sea downrange. Super Heavy and Ship, however, will steer themselves directly back to their launch tower, which will capture each vehicle with its "chopstick" arms.

This will allow SpaceX to inspect, refurbish and refly Starship at an accelerated rate, which is a priority for the company: Musk has said he envisions launching Starship more than 10,000 times per year by 2030.

Starship has conducted 14 test flights to date, and SpaceX has pulled off chopstick catches with Super Heavy on three of them. The company has not yet tried to catch Ship, which is a more difficult proposition, as the upper stage travels higher, farther and faster than the booster does.

Still, Musk is confident that SpaceX will pull off a Ship catch on the first try. (He did not give a specific target date for Flight 15, saying only that it was expected next month.)

"I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," he said. "And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year, and and then accelerating next year."

Success would mean back-to-back Starship flights with huge milestones. On Flight 14, which occurred on Sept. 28, Ship reached orbit for the first time ever. It also deployed 26 of SpaceX's Starlink Version 3 satellites — the first 26 members of a next-gen broadband constellation in low Earth orbit that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft.

The Starship Flight 15 preview was something of an aside during today's call. The event primarily served to announce SpaceX's financial performance during Q3, the three-month stretch that ended on Sept. 30.

And that performance was strong, company representatives said. SpaceX recorded revenues of $14.6 billion during Q3, an increase of 161% from the $5.6 billion earned during Q3 of 2025. The company had a net income of $4.4 billion during Q3, $5.5 billion better than the result from the same stretch last year, when SpaceX lost $1.1 billion.

Just $1.8 billion of 2026 Q3 revenue came from SpaceX's launch division. The vast majority was generated by two other segments — connectivity (services provided by its Starlink megaconstellation) and artificial intelligence (or, as the Trump administration has recently rebranded it, "superintelligence").

SpaceX thinks these latter two segments will continue to boom. That's why it's building the infrastructure to support thousands of Starship launches per year — to loft lots of Starlink satellites and AI data centers to Earth orbit. And the company believes that it's positioned to really start raking in the cash, starting as soon as next year.

"In a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of '27 is somewhere between 500 billion [dollars] and a trillion," Musk said.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 20, 1970: The Soviet Union launches last-ever Zond moon mission ]]>

On Oct. 20, 1970, the Soviet Union launched the Zond 8 spacecraft on a mission to the moon. This was the last mission in the Zond program.

After the first three Zond missions explored Venus and Mars, the next ones were circumlunar missions that flew around the moon before returning to Earth. Although there was no crew on board, the Zond spacecraft was designed with cosmonauts in mind.

The Zond missions served as test flights for the Soviet Union's plans to send cosmonauts to the moon. But those plans for crewed flights never came to fruition. This was partly because the U.S. had already put astronauts on the moon, but also because the Zond missions had a lot of technical problems.

Zond 8 was considered a success — even though its guidance system malfunctioned on the way back to Earth. The spacecraft still returned to Earth safely and splashed down in the Indian Ocean one week after it launched.

Why it mattered

While the Zond 1 and Zond 2 missions were launched toward Venus and Mars, respectively, the primary target of most Zond missions was the moon. At the time, the Soviet Union was embroiled in an ongoing space race with the United States to be the first on the moon with a human crew.

By the time Zond 8 launched on Oct. 20, 1970, that space race was lost to the Soviet Union. NASA and the U.S. had already landed astronauts on the moon twice with Apollo 11 and Apollo 12 (in July and November of 1969, respectively), and even peformed the first space rescue fo the Apollo 13 astronauts in April 1970.

While Zond 8 was uncrewed, it was a test flight of the Soviet Union's L1 spacecraft that was designed to fly a cosmonaut around the moon. It looped around the moon in a lunar flyby, approaching within 1,120 kilometers of the moon's surface at its closest point, according to RussianSpaceWeb.com.

Cameras on Zond 8 captured stunning views of the Earth and moon, recreating the iconic Earthrise views seen by Apollo 8 astronauts two years earlier in 1968.

Zond 8 ultimately splashed down in the Indian Ocean on Oct. 27, 1970 after a solar attitude sensor failed, sending it on a shorter, steeper reentry path during landing, according to RussianSpaceWeb.com. It was retrieved by a recovery ship, marking the end of the Soviet moon landing program. Russian would go on to develop a series of Salyut space stations, culminating in the long-lived Mir space station.

After decades without a moon probe, Russia did launch a new uncrewed moon lander in 2023. That Luna 25 mission failed and crashed into the lunar surface after an onboard engine controller malfunctioned. The country has pledged a return to the moon in 2027.

]]> <![CDATA[ Can’t make it to the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art for the 'Star Wars' display? This is the companion book set you’re looking for! ]]> Taschen, purveyors of fine art and design special-edition books, have teamed up with George Lucas and his newly opened Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles to present a masterful two-volume catalog of the museum’s illuminating offerings.

Housed in a sturdy slipcase, readers will discover a pair of lavishly illustrated volumes spanning 832 pages and tipping the scales at nearly 14 pounds. This immersive collection documents in great detail the astounding scope of rare items on display in Lucas’s treasury of paintings, murals, photographs, sculptures, posters, comic strips, illustrations, costumes, and magazine covers that have spurred humankind’s imagination.

Developed in collaboration with George Lucas and the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, this extensive two-volume catalog brings together an unparalleled collection of narrative art.View Deal

We'd absolutely recommend checking out the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in person if you can.

Our own Chelsea Gohd visited the Los Angeles-based museum ahead of its opening in September 2026 and adored it. But if you're not a California local, getting lost in this collection's glossy pages is the next best thing to roaming the museum exhibitions on a rainy afternoon.

Far beyond a mere companion to the marvels inside the fantastic spaceship-shaped building poised near the University of Southern California campus — the same institution where Lucas attended film school in the late 1960s — these bold editions are an adventure in their own right.

Waiting to be absorbed is an impressive assortment of storytelling expression that showcases beautiful works by everyone from Maxfield Parrish, N.C. Wyeth, and Norman Rockwell to Frank Frazetta, Jack Kirby, and Ralph McQuarrie. Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, curated the museum’s contents that represent decades of collecting narrative art in all of its forms.

]]> <![CDATA[ Jeff Bezos is playing the long game with Blue Origin (op-ed) ]]> Daniel Biedermann is a partner at NewSpace Capital. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights.

Jeff Bezos, the founder and former CEO of Amazon, recently said that Blue Origin, his space technology company, is likely to go public in the coming years. The announcement has (unsurprisingly) attracted considerable attention, not least because Bezos has spent more than two decades financing the company largely from his personal wealth. He has invested billions of dollars in developing rockets, spacecraft and other forms of technology, often with very little prospect of an immediate return. But although Bezos has now raised the possibility of an initial public offering, he has given no firm indication of when one might happen. He may be right to keep his options open.

Bezos founded Blue Origin in 2000. Because he has financed so much of its development by himself, the company has been able to pursue ambitious engineering projects without the financial pressures that publicly listed businesses typically face. But developing reusable rockets, manufacturing spacecraft and building the infrastructure needed for future lunar missions requires extraordinary amounts of capital: These projects can take decades to complete, and even the wealthiest investors must think hard about how best to finance them over the long term. Bezos, then, has good reasons to seek additional sources of investment — particularly as Blue Origin prepares to expand its commercial operations.

An IPO would give Blue Origin the means to raise substantial capital from public investors and reduce its dependence on Bezos's personal wealth. The company could then use that money to expand manufacturing, develop new technology and compete for a greater share of the growing space market. Public ownership would also give existing investors the power to sell some of their holdings and could make it easier for Blue Origin to finance acquisitions. But the company would also have to meet the expectations of shareholders, who would expect to see regular evidence of commercial progress. This, I suspect, is why Bezos wants to establish a stronger business before committing to a listing.

It might have much to prove commercially, but Blue Origin’s technical progress has been remarkable. In January 2025, its New Glenn rocket reached orbit for the first time — a significant achievement for a vehicle built to compete in the heavy-lift launch market. The company has also secured government and commercial contracts and continued developing its lunar capabilities. But it will eventually have to demonstrate that it can launch New Glenn frequently, reliably and at a commercially competitive cost, and it is still some way away from that point.

Some will be asking whether Bezos wants to raise money to accelerate growth or simply to reduce the amount he himself must invest. Such doubts could affect the company's valuation and make it harder to attract investors who share its long-term ambitions. But again, this suggests Bezos is playing the long game. And given the enthusiasm that has surrounded some billionaire-led space ventures, this is sensible. Investors have sometimes attached extraordinary valuations to companies with ambitious plans but limited commercial experience. Space businesses certainly require ambition: engineers will often spend years developing technology before they can sell it. But investors have to distinguish between technical achievement and commercial performance. At the end of the day, they are seeking a strong rate of return.

What’s also worth considering is how Blue Origin's progress could benefit the wider space industry, particularly the specialist companies that supply technology to larger manufacturers and operators. SpaceX has achieved remarkable success in part by developing and manufacturing much of its technology internally. This includes its rockets, spacecraft and satellites. Blue Origin also does something similar, undertaking substantial engineering and manufacturing work itself, but it is not quite so vertically integrated, and thus may have greater scope to work with external suppliers as it expands. It already buys parts, equipment and services from hundreds of businesses. If it can successfully increase its production and launch activity, these suppliers could receive more orders and gain opportunities to develop new technologies. That’s to the good of the sector as a whole.

Why? Because a successful space industry needs more than a handful of large launch providers. It needs companies specializing in satellite communications, propulsion, electronics, software and other areas. Such businesses may have developed highly sophisticated products, but they need bigger customers and predictable demand to expand and produce more. Blue Origin could become an important customer for some of these, particularly if it chooses to buy specialist technology rather than make everything internally. Greater competition between the bigger space companies could translate to more potential customers for suppliers and fewer dependent commercial relationships.

Investors would benefit. There’s real potential in businesses that provide the technology and services on which larger space companies depend — the ‘picks and shovels.’ These can sometimes serve several customers and markets, making them less dependent on the success of a single program. A growing Blue Origin would create more opportunities for companies like these — although, of course, much will depend on how Bezos chooses to organize its supply chain. We shouldn’t assume that Blue Origin will become more open to external suppliers than its competitors, but the possibility is at least worth entertaining.

As it is, Bezos still faces substantial challenges. Blue Origin is not yet a commercially mature business. The company must increase its launch activity; it must demonstrate its reliability; and it must compete for customers in the public and private sectors. It must also decide how much technology to manufacture internally and whether and where third parties can provide better products or products at a lower cost. Bezos has the resources to give the company time to answer these questions, and he appears to be willing to use them. If he continues to prioritize commercial performance before pursuing an IPO, then Blue Origin could eventually enter the public markets in a much stronger position.

]]> <![CDATA[ A supercomputer is about to launch to the moon aboard a rover named FLIP ]]> HAWTHORNE, Calif. — A moon buggy carrying a history-making supercomputer is ready to launch to the lunar surface. And it's taking some inspiration from Mars.

Later this year, Astrolab will launch its uncrewed moon rover FLIP to the lunar south pole as part of the Griffin Mission 1, or Griffin-1. The California company is one of two that NASA has selected to develop a drivable rover for the agency's Artemis program. On board FLIP will be Hewlett Packard Enterprise's (HPE) Spaceborne Computer-4, an advanced computer module built to be used in space.

This will be the first time that high-performance computing and artificial intelligence will be tested on the lunar surface. As NASA gets closer to landing humans back on the moon with Artemis, advancements like this aim to support future human habitation as well as economic activity on and around the moon.

"We're sending the first supercomputer from HPE to the lunar surface later this year, doing the first GPU [graphics processing unit] on the moon [and the] first AI experiments on the moon," Jaret Matthews, founder and CEO of Astrolab, said during an Oct. 14 media event here at Astrolab's headquarters. "They're breaking new ground, and they're ahead of the curve."

The computer is designed to be lightweight, compact, self-contained and fanless. It has a low-power 64-bit CPU (central processing unit) with a GPU. The computer will be attached to FLIP's cooling system and will be powered by a system supported by both batteries and solar cells on the rover. The computer will also be paired with solid state drives from the company KIOXIA that will allow for memory storage.

So, what will a supercomputer and AI accomplish on this uncrewed mission? First and foremost, the flightwill test how the computer works in this extreme environment. The computer is built with heat-conductive aluminum and is designed with the specific conditions of the lunar south pole in mind. But while it was designed and tested to be able to withstand the extreme temperatures and conditions on the moon's surface, the upcoming mission seeks to show that this advanced technology can actually work in this environment.

"NASA's given us a real challenge," Matthews told Space.com at the media event. "We have to design for a full year on the lunar surface. So that means surviving multiple lunar nights, upwards of 150 hours of complete darkness where we're not receiving energy or warmth from the sun. And then, also, there's going to be a long period [in] which we're operating semi-autonomously for [when] the astronauts are not there … and so we're having to develop a semi-autonomous platform that will spend many months [and] travel hundreds of kilometers [on the moon]."

But the computer will more than just prove its durability, if all goes to plan. It will also analyze visual data captured on the mission and enable autonomous observations, process navigation, mapping and terrain analysis. The mission also promises to test AI capabilities, though it's unclear what exact applications we'll see with this lunar AI. HPE shared in a statement that "an AI services container will demonstrate reliable deployment of scalable AI service applications on the moon."

It is also to be determined exactly how, once tested, these capabilities might be used with future crewed missions. Astronauts aboard the International Space Station already use computers for communications, science experiments and other daily tasks while living in space, but we can't say yet exactly how future astronauts might use these capabilities, especially with the addition of AI, on the moon.

From Mars to the moon

One interesting aspect of this new development is where it came from. While HPE has provided computing power to NASA for decades, Matthews is also bringing his previous experience working at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) into this new venture.

"One of the experiments [that will be] running on the spaceborne computer on the moon is a localization software experiment from JPL. It has been used on Mars, and this will be the first time it's used on the moon," Matthews said.

"The challenge with the moon and Mars is that there's no GPS, so locating yourself and knowing where you are on the surface [can be difficult]," he added. "So we're going to be running what is essentially a machine learning algorithm that JPL developed to take a map that's stored in memory … and compare it to the local terrain we see around us, and then do a match. So essentially, match features of the local terrain to the map that's stored in memory to help find ourselves on the map and keep ourselves away from dangerous craters."

As its name suggests, Griffin-1 will be the first mission for the robotic Griffin moon lander, which was developed by Astrobotic. The Pittsburgh company is flying Griffin-1 for NASA, under the agency's CLPS (Commercial Lunar Payload Services) program. In addition to FLIP, the mission will carry Astrobiotic's CubeRover, a small, uncrewed rover; LandCam-X, an optical navigation system; and Nanofiche GLPH (Galactic Library to Preserve Humanity), a tiny archive of human history, to the moon's surface.

"The moon presents a challenging environment for advanced computing, and we’re pleased to provide HPE with an opportunity to demonstrate its technology on the lunar surface," Matthews added in a statement. "Our FLIP rover is designed to accommodate a variety of payloads, and this mission will demonstrate how commercial lunar mobility platforms can support technology development and scientific research."

]]> <![CDATA[ Red light, white light: How to preserve your night vision while using stargazing apps ]]> The best stargazing apps can take your observation of the night sky to the next level, whether that's using augmented reality (AR mode) to identify stars or looking up the next lunar eclipse.

However, the bright light emitted by smartphone screens can prevent your eyes from adjusting to the dark. If you're using one of the best telescopes, you'll want to preserve your night vision even more. Fortunately, there are ways to all but eliminate this problem.

Why are bright screens bad for stargazing?

When you step out into the dark, it can take up to 20-30 minutes for your vision to adjust. The rod cells in your eyes build up a chemical known as rhodopsin, which gives you night vision.

However, bright light bleaches that chemical, negatively impacting your night vision. So when you look through a telescope, binoculars or just turn your eyes to the night sky after peering at a bright phone screen, it'll be harder for you to pick out fainter objects such as galaxies and nebulas.

One way of fixing this problem is simply to put your phone away and wait another 20-30 minutes. But if you're using a stargazing app to help you navigate the night skies, that's not really an option.

The good news is that, between individual stargazing apps and your phone's own built-in features, you can minimize the impact of your smartphone's screen light.

How to block white light in stargazing apps

Many of the best stargazing apps will let you enable a red light filter or similar, though this option may not always be present in the free version. Here's how to do that in three of our favorite stargazing apps:

SkyView: Tap the screen, tap the horizontal lines, tap on Settings, then Display, then Night Mode and Red.

Star Walk 2: Tap the horizontal lines, tap on Settings, then tap the button next to Night Mode.

Sky Tonight: Tap the horizontal lines, tap on Settings, then Tools, then Night Mode.

All these modes will minimize the amount of white light coming from the app. However, be aware that this is only within the app. Once you go back to your phone's main menu, it will be at full color. With the red screen naturally looking darker, you may have turned up the brightness on your phone, so making the switch away from the app will be quite the shock.

If you want to dim your whole phone or put it into red light mode, here's how to do that on Android or iPhone.

How to block white light on Android phones

On Android, there are several ways to minimize the impact of bright light, depending on the model and make of phone you have.

One near-universal option is to dim your smartphone. Swipe down the notification panel from the top of the screen and you'll see a brightness slider. Slide this to the left to dim your phone.

We'd also recommend disabling adaptive brightness in the Display section of your phone's settings. You may also have an Extra Dim option in the Accessibility menu — just don't dim the screen to the point of not being able to see it at all!

Some Android phones, such as recent Samsung and Google Pixel models, also offer a Red Filter. On some, you'll find this in Accessibility, then Vision Enhancements, then Color Filter. You can then choose the color you want and also tweak the opacity.

All the above options will let you continue to use your smartphone for stargazing, while minimizing its negative impact on your night vision.

How to block white light on Apple iPhones

As with Android phones, iPhones have a built-in option to dim the screen brightness. In this case, you swipe down from the top of the screen and look for the vertical brightness slider, represented by a sun icon. Reduce the slider as much as you're comfortable with, dimming the screen while still keeping it visible.

Beyond that, recent iPhones also offer the ability to apply a color filter, again via their Accessibility options. Here's how to do that.

First, tap on the Settings icon, then pick Accessibility. Select Display & Text Size and go to Color Filters. Tap the Color Filter button. Then, pick Color Tint and move the Hue and Intensity sliders all the way to the right.

With the red screen naturally looking darker, you may have turned up the brightness on your phone, so making the switch away from the app will be quite the shock.

If you want to dim your whole phone or put it into red light mode, here's how to do that on Android or iPhone.

How to block white light on Android phones

On Android, there are several ways to minimize the impact of bright light, depending on the model and make of phone you have.

One near-universal option is to dim your smartphone. Swipe down the notification panel from the top of the screen and you'll see a brightness slider. Slide this to the left to dim your phone.

We'd also recommend disabling adaptive brightness in the Display section of your phone's settings. You may also have an Extra Dim option in the Accessibility menu — just don't dim the screen to the point of not being able to see it at all!

Some Android phones, such as recent Samsung and Google Pixel models, also offer a Red Filter. On some, you'll find this in Accessibility, then Vision Enhancements, then Color Filter. You can then choose the color you want and also tweak the opacity.

All the above options will let you continue to use your smartphone for stargazing, while minimizing its negative impact on your night vision.

How to block white light on Apple iPhones

As with Android phones, iPhones have a built-in option to dim the screen brightness. In this case, you swipe down from the top of the screen and look for the vertical brightness slider, represented by a sun icon. Reduce the slider as much as you're comfortable with, dimming the screen while still keeping it visible.

Beyond that, recent iPhones also offer the ability to apply a color filter, again via their Accessibility options. Here's how to do that.

First, tap on the Settings icon, then pick Accessibility. Select Display & Text Size and go to Color Filters. Tap the Color Filter button. Then, pick Color Tint and move the Hue and Intensity sliders all the way to the right.

]]> <![CDATA[ The view from the edge of a sparkling spiral galaxy | Space photo of the day for Oct. 20, 2026 ]]>

If you were approaching the edge of a spiral galaxy, arriving from afar through the cosmos, it might look something like this.

What is it?

In this new snapshot by the Hubble Space Telescope's Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS), we can see the edge of the spiral galaxy NGC 1827. Found about 37 million light-years from Earth, this galaxy sparkles in this side-on view.

Not all spiral galaxies are the same. This galaxy is what is known as an "intermediate" spiral, which means that its structure sits somewhere between that of a barred and unbarred spiral galaxy. Barred galaxies have a distinctive central, bar-shaped structure, while the unbarred variety lacks this bar and can look more like circular spirals.

NGC 1827's spiral shape isn't clear from the side, however. From this perspective, we see its twinkling edge, speckled with stars and woven together with brown ribbons of dust.

Why is it incredible?

Beneath the beauty of this spiral edge lies an expansive, cosmic landscape. Bright blue stars dot the spiral's side, with one particularly luminous star taking the spotlight with four diffraction spikes — created by light bending through the inner workings of Hubble's camera — emanating from its center.

This image was captured as part of a larger Hubble survey that's exploring 260 satellite galaxies, which are galaxies gravitationally bound to larger hosts. Hubble is specifically looking to survey satellite galaxies that lie near host galaxies similar to our own Milky Way.

So far, Hubble has spotted 111 such satellites and will continue to observe, hunting for the rest.

By studying satellite galaxies like this one, which also happens to be an especially low-mass galaxy, researchers could better understand the complicated dynamics both within the galaxies themselves and between them and their host galaxies.

 <description>Pražský městský soud ve středu uložil někdejšímu předsedovi představenstva společnosti Amun.Re Martinu Shenarovi viněnému z rozsáhlých daňových úniků při prodeji tří společností firmě ČEZ peněžitý trest 7,2 milionu korun. <link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/restauracni-restart-podruhe-znamy-gastrostartup-sveruje-provozy-umele-inteligenci/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český startup Choice, který funguje v desítkách tisíc restaurací jako technologická platforma pro online objednávky, rezervace a marketing, nově nechá umělou inteligenci provádět změny v provozu. AI bude na pokyn restauratéra sama konat, upraví třeba menu a ceny, spustí marketingovou kampaň nebo vytvoří nový web. Systém zakladatel a &#353;éf Choice Alex Ilyash rozbíhá s mohutnou podporou investice 7,1 milionu dolarů (přes 150 milionů Kč) z leto&#353;ního března a reaguje na změny na SaaS trhu.</description>

<item>
<title>Jak zvládnout nový zákon o kyberbezpečnosti? Stát ukázal, jak správně nastavit řízení rizik</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/jak-zvladnout-novy-zakon-o-kyberbezpecnosti-stat-ukazal-jak-spravne-nastavit-rizeni-rizik/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Národní úřad pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost (NÚKIB) vydal nové podpůrné materiály pro subjekty spadající pod nový zákon o kybernetické bezpečnosti.  <description>Detektivové protikorupčního úřadu Ukrajiny (NABU) provádějí razii v sídle ukrajinské centrální banky. Stejně tak provádějí domovní prohlídku u jednoho ze zaměstnanců banky. Úřad to potvrdil na platformě Telegram. Na prohlídky dohlíží speciální protikorupční prokuratura (SAP). Poslanec Oleksij Hončarenko napsal, že NABU provádí vyšetřování v kanceláři guvernéra banky Andrije Pyšného a na dalších místech, která jsou s ním spojená.</description>

Kudy z nudy – Žebříčky: Liberecký kraj Žebříčky RSS Feed <![CDATA[Křišťálové Vánoce u Liebiegů]]>

Křišťálové Vánoce u Liebiegů nabídnou setkání tvůrců z Křišťálového údolí i dalších regionů na jednom místě. Čeká vás pestrá přehlídka sklářských výrobků, tradičních řemesel, autorského designu a poctivých regionálních produktů.

]]> Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:03:51 GMT <![CDATA[Café Union v České Lípě]]>

Café Union v historickém centru České Lípy zve na snídaně, obědy, výběrovou kávu a zákusky z vlastní cukrářské výroby. Kavárna zaujme interiérem laděným do secese. V patře nabízí také společenský sál pro soukromé a firemní akce.

]]> Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:49 GMT <![CDATA[Svatomartinská husa na Rychtě Jestřebí]]>

Přijďte si užít svatého Martina v klidu a pohodě k nám na Rychtu! Od 11. do 15. listopadu 2026 jsme pro vás připravili speciální sezónní menu. Všechno jsme upekli a uvěřili s láskou tak, aby vám u stolu bylo jednoduše dobře.

]]> Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:41:53 GMT <![CDATA[Dlabání dýní na Rychtě]]>

Už jste někdy nechali děti dlabat dýně v obýváku? Semínkový teror všude okolo je přesně ten důvod, proč se do toho doma raději nepouštět. Přijďte v neděli k nám! Připravili jsme správně velké dýně, které se dětem dobře dlabou, a jejich úklid zůstane na nás.

]]> Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:31:43 GMT

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>Nová éra ikonické stavby: Technikův pavilon v Liberci ožívá jako infocentrum</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903639-nova-era-ikonicke-stavby-technikuv-pavilon-v-liberci-oziva-jako-infocentrum.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903639-nova-era-ikonicke-stavby-technikuv-pavilon-v-liberci-oziva-jako-infocentrum.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Kultura</category><description>V Liberci byla slavnostně otevřena replika Technikova pavilonu z roku 1946. Bývalý výstavištní objekt známý i pod názvem Casino nahradila moderní nízkoenergetická replika, která se stane zázemím pro nové městské infocentrum, kulturní akce, přednášky, výstavy a nabídne i veřejné toalety.</description></item><item><title>Vánoční zázrak v Jablonci: Objevte lesk 9 000 skleněných ozdob</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903577-vanocni-zazrak-v-jablonci-objevte-lesk-9-000-sklenenych-ozdob.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kultura/903577-vanocni-zazrak-v-jablonci-objevte-lesk-9-000-sklenenych-ozdob.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 13:02:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Kultura</category><description>Připravte se na pořádnou dávku svátečního třpytu! Jablonecké muzeum skla a bižuterie otevírá 23. října nový návštěvnický depozitář s největší výstavou vánočních ozdob na světě nazvanou Svět fantazie. Čeká na vás až 9 000 křehkých skvostů, historických unikátů i pohádkový kočár z foukaných perlí.</description></item><item><title>Do Jablonce míří fanoušci Brightonu, na stadion půjdou neorganizovaně</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903597-do-jablonce-miri-fanousci-brightonu-na-stadion-pujdou-neorganizovane.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903597-do-jablonce-miri-fanousci-brightonu-na-stadion-pujdou-neorganizovane.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:34:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Na jabloneckou střelnici míří aktuálně jeden z nejlepších anglických klubů z Brightonu. Ten je třetí v Premier League, pro domácí tak půjde o těžkou zkoušku. Na sever Čech navíc dorazí stovky anglických fanoušků, na což se připravuje i policie.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký hejtman Martin Půta chce funkci předat do konce roku, adeptů je víc</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903586-liberecky-hejtman-martin-puta-chce-funkci-predat-do-konce-roku-adeptu-je.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903586-liberecky-hejtman-martin-puta-chce-funkci-predat-do-konce-roku-adeptu-je.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 08:34:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Liberecký hejtman Martin Půta ze Starostů pro Liberecký kraj (SLK) chce svému nástupci funkci předat do konce letošního roku. Adeptů na místo hejtmana je víc, rozhodovat tak bude zřejmě sněm, řekl po dnešním jednání krajského zastupitelstva Půta.</description></item><item><title>Do libereckého bazénu se vrací ikonická červená mozaika. Vyrábí ji v Desné</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903574-do-libereckeho-bazenu-se-vraci-ikonicka-cervena-mozaika-vyrabi-ji-v-desne.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903574-do-libereckeho-bazenu-se-vraci-ikonicka-cervena-mozaika-vyrabi-ji-v-desne.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Rozsáhlá rekonstrukce libereckého bazénu přináší i obnovu jeho ikonického vzhledu. Původní červenou mozaiku nahradí věrná nová kopie, pro kterou v Desné vyrábějí 19 milionů skleněných kostiček. V Preciose Ornelle tak oživili historickou technologii, s níž v závodě dosud neměli zkušenost.</description></item><item><title>Tygři mají bod z Vítkovic. Po nájezdech prohráli 2:3</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/903566-tygri-maji-bod-z-vitkovic-po-najezdech-prohrali-2-3.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/903566-tygri-maji-bod-z-vitkovic-po-najezdech-prohrali-2-3.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 20:21:18 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Stejně jako v Brně, i ve Vítkovicích Tygři prohráli 2:3, tentokrát ne v prodloužení, ale po nájezdech. A také nyní vyrovnávali v závěru základní hrací doby na 2:2.</description></item><item><title>Nezvládáte vztek? V Jablonci funguje centrum, které vám pomůže změnit život</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903490-nezvladate-vztek-v-jablonci-funguje-centrum-ktere-vam-pomuze-zmenit-zivot.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903490-nezvladate-vztek-v-jablonci-funguje-centrum-ktere-vam-pomuze-zmenit-zivot.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Vztek a agresi ve vztazích se lze naučit zvládat. Regionální terapeutické centrum Stop násilí nabízí odbornou pomoc i obyvatelům Libereckého kraje, a to v Jablonci nad Nisou. Až 79 % klientů potvrzuje, že díky terapii dokázali své reakce změnit. Zjistěte, jaký udělali první krok.</description></item><item><title>Sezónní deprese není jen podzimní splín. Vyhledat pomoc včas má smysl</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903479-sezonni-deprese-neni-jen-podzimni-splin-vyhledat-pomoc-vcas-ma-smysl.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903479-sezonni-deprese-neni-jen-podzimni-splin-vyhledat-pomoc-vcas-ma-smysl.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:54:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Viktorie Beránková</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Péče o duševní zdraví není jen otázkou podzimu. Právě kratší dny a změna denního režimu ale mohou u některých lidí zhoršit psychickou pohodu. Jak poznat běžný podzimní splín od sezónní deprese, která už zasahuje do každodenního života?</description></item><item><title>Chřipková sezóna klepe na dveře: Proč letos očkování nepodcenit?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903488-chripkova-sezona-klepe-na-dvere-proc-letos-ockovani-nepodcenit.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903488-chripkova-sezona-klepe-na-dvere-proc-letos-ockovani-nepodcenit.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>S příchodem podzimu opět sílí riziko respiračních infekcí a chřipky, která může mít závažné následky. Říjen a listopad představují ideální čas pro prevenci. Zjistěte, pro koho je očkování zdarma, jak se účinně chránit a na co si dát pozor při prvních příznacích.</description></item><item><title>KVÍZ: Dýně i české zvyky. Vyznáte se v podzimních tradicích?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kvizy/903477-kviz-dyne-i-ceske-zvyky-vyznate-se-v-podzimnich-tradicich.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kvizy/903477-kviz-dyne-i-ceske-zvyky-vyznate-se-v-podzimnich-tradicich.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 20 Oct 2026 12:12:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Nicolas Rosier</dc:creator><category>Kvízy</category><description>Vydlabané dýně, strašidelné kostýmy i vzpomínky na zesnulé blízké. Podzim se pojí s různými tradicemi, které mají překvapivě pestrou historii. Víte, odkud pochází Halloween, co se slaví v Mexiku a na kdy připadají české Dušičky? Otestujte se v našem kvízu.</description></item></channel></rss>

 <description><p>
	<strong>V sobotu 10. října se sklářská huť Preciosa v Kamenickém Šenově opět otevře festivalovému publiku. Benefiční projekt V žáru žen nabídne hudbu Beaty Hlavenkové, HRTL a Oskara Töröka, laserovou performance Davida Vrbíka i práci se sklem. Výtěžek večera a tichá aukce podpoří Nadační fond Ozvěna, který pomáhá dětem s trvalou ztrátou sluchu.</strong></p>
